translations.text: Paul, an apostle—not from human beings or through a human being, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead—
and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia:
Grace to you and peace from God the Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ.
who gave himself for our sins to rescue us from this evil world, according to the will of our God and Father,
to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
I am astonished that you are so quickly turning away from the one who called you in the grace of Christ to a different gospel.
There is no other gospel, but there are some who trouble you and want to distort the gospel of Christ.
But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach to you anything beyond what we preached to you, let him be accursed.
As we said before, so now I say again: If anyone preaches to you anything beyond what you received, let him be accursed.
Am I now to please human beings or God? Or am I seeking to please human beings? If I were still pleasing human beings, I would not be a servant of Christ.
I make known to you, brothers, that the gospel I preached is not of human origin.
For I neither received it from a human being nor learned it from anyone, but through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
For you have heard about my former conduct in Judaism, how I persecuted the church of God beyond measure and ravaged it.
I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my peers among my people, being especially zealous for my ancestral traditions.
But when God, who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me through his grace, was pleased
to reveal his Son in me so that I might proclaim him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately consult flesh and blood,
nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me. Instead, I went to Arabia and returned again to Damascus.
Then, after three years, I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter and stayed with him for fifteen days.
I saw no other apostle except James, the Lord's brother.
As for what I am writing to you, behold, before God, I am not lying.
Then I came to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
I was unknown by sight to the churches of the circumcised who were in Christ.
They had only heard, "The one who persecuted us then is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy."
And they glorified God because of me.
Then, after fourteen years, I went up to Jerusalem again with Barnabas, taking Titus with me as well.
I went up in response to the revelation and laid before them the gospel I was preaching among the Gentiles, privately before those held in esteem, lest I had run or might run in vain.
But even Titus, who was with me and was a Gentile, was not compelled to be circumcised.
But because of the false brothers who slipped in, who sneaked in to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus so that they might enslave us—
we did not yield to them in submission even for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel might remain firmly established among you.
But as for those regarded as important—whatever they once were makes no difference to me, for God shows no favoritism—those regarded as important imparted nothing of that kind to me.
On the contrary, when they saw that I had been entrusted with the gospel for the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been for the circumcised,
for the one who enabled Peter to serve as an apostle to the circumcised also enabled me to serve among the Gentiles,

when James, Cephas, and John, who were regarded as pillars, recognized the grace that had been given to me, they gave me and Barnabas their hands in agreement, so that we would go to the Gentiles and they to the circumcised.
They asked only that we remember the poor, which I myself was eager to do.
But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him, because [?] he was, as it were, condemned.
For before certain people came from James, he ate freely with the Gentiles. But when they came, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing those who belonged to the circumcised.
The other Jews also joined him in hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas yielded to their hypocrisy.

But when I saw that they were not walking rightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas before everyone, “If you, though you are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”
For we are Jews by birth, and not sinners from among the Gentiles.

We know that a person is not justified by works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ. We too believed in Christ Jesus so that we might be justified through faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because no one will be justified by works of the law.
But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, then has Christ become a servant of sin? Certainly not!
For if I rebuild what they tore down, I myself show that I am a transgressor.
For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live for God.
And I was crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.
And I do not reject the grace of God, for if righteousness came through the law, then Christ died for nothing.
O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was portrayed as though crucified before you?
I want to learn only this from you: did you receive the Spirit through works of the law or through hearing with faith?
Are you so foolish? Having begun with the Spirit, are you now finishing with the flesh?
Did you undergo so much in vain—if indeed it was in vain?
Now, did the one who gave you the Spirit and worked miracles among you do so through works of the law or through hearing with faith?
Just as Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
Do you therefore know that those who live by faith are the children of Abraham?
Scripture knew beforehand that God would justify the Gentiles through faith. God promised Abraham beforehand, “In you all nations will be blessed.”
So those who live by faith are blessed along with Abraham, who believed.
For all who rely on works of the law are under a curse, for it is written, “Cursed is everyone who does not abide by everything written in the book of the law, to do it all.”
It is clear that no one is justified before God by the law, for it says, “The righteous will live by faith.”
But the law is not based on faith; rather, whoever does these things will live by them.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us, for it is written, “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree,”
so that the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, and so that we might receive the promise of the Holy Spirit through faith.
Brothers, I speak in human terms: even a human covenant, once confirmed, cannot be set aside by anyone, nor can any further provision be added to it.
The promises were made to Abraham and his descendant. He does not say “descendants,” as though referring to many, but refers to one: “And to your descendant,” who is Christ.
But this is what I mean: the law, which was established four hundred and thirty years later, cannot overturn the covenant previously confirmed by God in Christ, so as to cancel the promise.
If the inheritance comes from the law, then it no longer comes from the promise. But God graciously gave it to Abraham through a promise.
What, then, is the law for? It was added because of transgressions, until the offspring should come to whom the promise had been made. It was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.
Now a mediator is not for just one party, but God is one.
Is the law, then, opposed to the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that could bring life, then righteousness would indeed have come from the law.
But Scripture confined everyone under sin, so that the promise that comes through faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
Before faith came, we were kept under guard, confined under the law until the coming faith that was to be revealed in us.
Thus the law became our tutor leading us to Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by faith.
But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a tutor.
For you are all sons of God through faith in Jesus Christ.
All of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ. There is no distinction
between Jew and Gentile, slave and free, male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s offspring, heirs according to the promise.
This is what I mean: as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, although he is master of everything.
Rather, he is under stewards and governors until the time appointed by his father.
Likewise, when we were children, we were enslaved under the elements of this world.
But when the fullness of time came, God sent his Son, who was born of a woman and came under the law,
to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons.
And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, “Abba, Father!”
So you are no longer a slave but a son, and if a son, then also an heir of God.
But at that time, when you did not know God, you served those who by nature were not gods.
But now you know God—or rather, you are known by God. How can you turn back again to the weak and impoverished elements, to which you want to enslave yourselves once more?
You observe days and months and seasons and years.
I fear for you, lest I have labored among you in vain.
Become like me, for I too was like you. Brothers, I beg you. You have done me no wrong.
You know that it was because of bodily weakness that I first preached the good news to you, and the trials that were in my body
you did not despise or scorn. Instead, you received me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
Where, then, is your blessedness now? I testify that, if it had been possible, you would have taken out your eyes and given them to me.
So have I become your enemy because I spoke the truth?
They stir up your zeal, but not for a good purpose. They want to exclude you so that you will be zealous for them.
But it is good to be zealous for good things at all times, and not only when I am among you.
My little children, for whom I am again in labor until Christ is formed in you!
I would like to come to you now and change my tone, for I am perplexed about you.
Tell me, you who want to be under the law: have you not read the law?
For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and one by the free woman.
But the one by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, and the one by the free woman through the promise.
This is an allegory, for these are two covenants: one from Mount Sinai, giving birth to slavery, which is Hagar.
For Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to this Jerusalem, for she is enslaved along with her children.
But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is the mother of us all.
For it is written: “Rejoice, barren woman who did not bear children! Cry out and shout, you who were not in labor! For the deserted woman has more children than the woman who has a husband.”
But we, brothers, are children of the promise, like Isaac.
But just as at that time the one born according to the flesh persecuted the one born according to the Spirit, so it is now.
But what does Scripture say? “Cast out the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman's son must not inherit with the free woman's son.”
Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman but of the free woman, through the freedom with which Christ has set us free.
Stand firm from now on, and do not come under the yoke of slavery again.
Look, I, Paul, tell you that if you are circumcised, Christ will be of no help to you.
I testify to every man who is circumcised that he is obligated to fulfill the whole law.
You who seek to be justified by the law have been cut off from Christ and have fallen away from grace.
For through the Spirit, by faith, we await the hope of righteousness.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any power, but faith working through love.
You were running well. Who stopped you from obeying the truth?
For that persuasion does not come from the one who called you.
A little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough.
But I am confident in you through the Lord that you will not think differently. Whoever is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.
But, brothers, if I were preaching circumcision, why am I still persecuted? Then the stumbling block of the cross would have been removed.
I wish those who trouble you would even castrate themselves!
For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not let your freedom become an opportunity for the flesh, but serve one another through love.
For the whole law is fulfilled in one saying: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
But if you bite and devour one another, be careful that you are not destroyed by one another.
But I say this: Walk by the Spirit, and do not fulfill the desire of the flesh.
For the flesh desires what is contrary to the Spirit, and the Spirit what is contrary to the flesh. Because these oppose one another, you do not do whatever you want.
But if you are led by the Spirit, then you are not under the law.
For the works of the flesh are evident, namely: adultery, sexual immorality, impurity, lust,
idolatry, sorcery, hostility, strife, jealousy, anger, rivalries, divisions, factions,
envy, murders, drunkenness, debauchery, and anything like these. I warn you beforehand, as I told you before, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
But the fruit of the Spirit is this: love, joy, peace, patience.
Kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, self-control. The law is not against such things.
But those who belong to Christ have crucified their flesh, together with its passions and desires.
If we live by the Spirit, let us also keep in step with the Spirit.
And let us not become conceited, challenging one another and envying one another.
Brothers, if anyone among you is suddenly caught in any transgression, you who are spiritual should restore such a person in a spirit of gentleness. Watch yourselves, so that you too are not tempted.
Bear one another’s burdens, and in this way fulfill the law of Christ.
If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
Let each person examine his own work, and then he will have grounds for boasting in himself alone, and not in comparison with his neighbor.
For each person will carry their own burden.
Let the student share all good things with the teacher.
Do not be deceived: God is not mocked.
For whatever a person sows, that they will also reap. Whoever sows to their own flesh will reap corruption from the flesh, and whoever sows to the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
But let us not grow weary of doing good, for we will reap at the proper time if we do not give up.
So, while we have time, let us do good to everyone, especially to those who belong to the household of faith.
See what kind of letters I have written to you with my own hand.
All those who want to make a good impression in the flesh compel you to be circumcised, only so that they may not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.
For even those who are circumcised do not keep the law, but they want you to be circumcised so that they may boast in your flesh.
But far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is anything, but a new creation.
And peace and mercy be upon all who conform to this rule, and upon the Israel of God.
From now on, let no one trouble me, for I bear the sufferings of Christ in my body.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen. To the Galatians, written from Rome.
